column1: # The names a catalogue index keeps, and which decoders open each one.
# **One list, read by both runtimes** (`GOAL.md` round 8, item 1). The phone's copy is
# moment the two disagree, so a name added on one side and not the other cannot ship. The page reads
# this file at run time and keeps a name only if **at least one of its decoders is in the engine it
# is running on** -- which is how the browser, whose build has no ZXTune, comes to index 61% of
# Modland rather than all of it.
# A decoder is judged absent only when the engine says so: `pt_backends` ends in `zxtune:none` when
# that decoder is compiled out, and names nothing else as missing. HivelyTracker is in every build
# and is not in the fingerprint at all, so "not mentioned" must mean "present" -- the rule is the
# engine's absence, never this file's guess.
# Two names have two decoders, and that is not a mistake: `fc` is the Amiga Future Composer to
# libopenmpt and an Atari 8-bit format to ASAP; `psm` is Epic MegaGames to libopenmpt and Pro Sound
# Maker to ZXTune. Either decoder being present keeps the name.
# ZX Spectrum -- the rows the browser build cannot open
# Filename prefixes, the Amiga way: `mod.title` rather than `title.mod`
